ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The M line at the bottom of the figure represents the Earth's surface. Jia is near the ground at the lower left, and Yi is near the ground at the lower right; Bing is at the upper left, and Ding is at the upper right. On the right side of the figure there is an airflow from Ding downward pointing to Yi, numbered ②; at the bottom there is a near-surface airflow moving from Yi toward Jia, numbered ③; on the left side there is an airflow moving upward from Jia, numbered ④; at the top there is an airflow moving from Bing toward Ding, numbered ①. Then reason: The question asks which airflow the formation of the high pressure at Yi in the low-latitude circulation is related to. Near-surface high pressure is usually formed when air descends and then accumulates and increases pressure near the ground. In the figure, the descending airflow above Yi is airflow ② descending from Ding to Yi. Therefore, the formation of the high pressure at Yi is related to airflow ②.
